newsitem.title: USA: Reading & Bates sets dry hole writeoff.
newsitem.headline: Reading & Bates sets dry hole writeoff.

text.p: Reading & Bates Corp said Wednesday it will take a second quarter writeoff of about $7.3 million to reflect its costs in the Ewing Bank No.1 well under the successful effort accounting method.

The Emerald prospect well in deep water offshore Louisana was drilled to a depth of 10,400 feet before being plugged and abandoned. It is jointly owned by Reading & Bates and the operator, Santa Fe Energy Resources Inc.
Another Gulf of Mexico well operated by Santa Fe, Garden Banks 372 No. 1, has been temporarily abandoned pending further drilling in the immediate area, Reading & Bates said.
Owners of the Knight prospect well are Santa Fe Energy, with 50 percent; and Reading and Bares and the Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shell Offshore, 25 percent each.

Reading & Bates said it and Santa Fe agreed for Shell Offshore to acquire and evaluate additional 3-D seismic to further define a deeper prospect on the block, offshore Louisiana. Shell will operate and own a 60 percent working interest in the deep prospect with Development and Santa Fe equally sharing the remaining interest.

Reading & Bates and Santa Fe plan to start the third well in their seven well joint venture program on the Amundsen prospect on East Breaks 335 in early July. In addition, they will participate in a Shell operated well on the Jalopeno prospect on Garden Banks 370 later this month.
